The test image shows a corn leaf with a single oval lesion — tan/gray center with a distinct yellow halo surrounding it. The lesion is small and discrete, on an otherwise green leaf.

This pattern strongly suggests **Eyespot** (small oval lesions with tan centers and yellow halos) as the top candidate. Let me verify with a reference.

The Eyespot reference shows many tiny circular spots scattered across the leaf — quite different from the test image which has a single larger oval lesion (~2-3cm) with a tan/gray center and pronounced yellow halo.

That single oval lesion with a yellow halo is more consistent with **Holcus Spot** (caused by bacterial infection, producing discrete oval lesions with tan centers and yellow halos), not Eyespot (which produces many tiny scattered circular spots).
